items.title: 6.1.3 Working Rule to Find the Centre and Radius of a Circle in General Form (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 166-167: working rule Steps 1-3 for centre and radius from the general form; Example 3 (5x^2 + 5y^2 + 20x + 25y + 10 = 0); Example 4 (locus PA^2 + PB^2 = 4)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne saabit kiya ke \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) ka centre \((-g, -f)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\) hai. Ab isi baat ko ek aasaan 'working rule' (kaam ka qaida) bana dete hain, taa ke exam mein foran centre aur radius nikal sakein. Kitab ke teen steps yeh hain:
Step 1: Agar zaroorat ho to \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 banayein: poori equation ko \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke common coefficient se divide kar dein.

blocks.text_alt: Centre equals (minus coefficient of x over 2, minus coefficient of y over 2)

blocks.latex: r = \sqrt{\begin{aligned}&\left(\dfrac{\text{coeff. of } x}{2}\right)^{2} + \left(\dfrac{\text{coeff. of } y}{2}\right)^{2} \\ &- \text{constant term}\end{aligned}}
blocks.text_alt: Radius equals the square root of: (coefficient of x over 2) squared plus (coefficient of y over 2) squared minus the constant term

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh qaida asal mein Theorem 2 hi hai, bas lafzon mein. \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) mein \(x\) ka coefficient \(2g\) hai, is liye \(g = \frac{\text{coeff. of } x}{2}\), aur centre ka pehla coordinate \(-g\) hai. \(y\) ke liye bhi yahi. Constant term \(c\) hai, is liye radius \(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\) bilkul Step 3 hai.
Step 1 ko kabhi na bhooliye: yeh qaida tabhi chalta hai jab \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 hon. Agar woh masalan 5 hain, to pehle har term ko 5 se divide kijiye.
Aur agar Step 3 mein root ke andar wala number zero ya negative aaye, to asal circle nahin banta (point circle ya imaginary circle, 6.1.2 ka Note).
Ek chhota sa yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'aadha karo, sign badlo: centre; aadhon ke square jama karo, constant ghatao, root lo: radius.'

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 10x + 4y + 4 = 0\) ka centre aur radius? (Aadha karo, sign badlo: centre \((5, -2)\). Radius \(\sqrt{25 + 4 - 4} = 5\).)

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Equation \(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} + 20x + 25y + 10 = 0\) represents a circle. Find its centre and radius.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} + 20x + 25y + 10 = 0\).
Maloom karna: is circle ka centre aur radius.
Tareeqa: working rule. Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients kya hain: dono 5 hain. Is liye pehla kaam Step 1 hai (5 se divide), phir general form se muqabla.

Step 1: Squares ke coefficients 1 banayein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x + 5y + 2 = 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
Kyun: general form \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) mein \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 hai. Har term ko 5 se divide karne se equation wahi rehti hai (right side zero hai, \(0 / 5 = 0\)).
Dhyan dein: sirf \(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) ko nahin, har term ko divide karna hai: \(20x / 5 = 4x\), \(25y / 5 = 5y\), \(10 / 5 = 2\).

Step 2: General form se muqabla
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
\[2g = 4 \Rightarrow g = 2\]
\[2f = 5 \Rightarrow f = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
\[c = 2\]
Kyun: (i) aur (ii) ke milte julte terms barabar karne se \(g\), \(f\) aur \(c\) mil jate hain. \(f\) fraction aaya to ghabraiye mat, yeh bilkul theek hai.

Step 3: Centre
\[(-g, -f) = \left(-2, -\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: Theorem 2 ke mutabiq centre coefficients ka aadha hai, sign badal kar.

Step 4: Radius
\[r = \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\]
\[= \sqrt{(2)^{2} + \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^{2} - 2}\]
\[= \sqrt{4 + \dfrac{25}{4} - 2} = \sqrt{2 + \dfrac{25}{4}}\]
\[= \sqrt{\dfrac{8 + 25}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{33}}{2}\]
Kyun: Theorem 2 ka radius formula. Andar wala number \(\frac{33}{4}\) positive hai, is liye yeh asal (real) circle hai. \(2 = \frac{8}{4}\) likh kar fractions jama kiye, aur \(\sqrt{4} = 2\) neeche nikal aaya.

Tasdeeq:
Standard form banayein: \((x + 2)^{2} + \left(y + \frac{5}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{33}{4}\). Kholne par:
\[x^{2} + 4x + 4 + y^{2} + 5y + \dfrac{25}{4} = \dfrac{33}{4}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x + 5y + 2 = 0\]
Yeh wahi (i) hai, aur 5 se multiply karne par di hui equation wapas mil jati hai. Jawab durust.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 3 se humne kya seekha? Teen baatein:
1. Pehla qadam hamesha coefficients ko dekhna hai. Agar \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke saath 5 laga hai to pehle 5 se divide; is ke baghair aage barhna sab se mehngi ghalti hai, kyun ke phir centre aur radius dono ghalat aate hain.
2. \(g\) aur \(f\) fractions bhi ho sakte hain (yahan \(f = \frac{5}{2}\)). Fractions se darna nahin, bas squares aur jama dhyan se karein.
3. Aakhir mein jawab ko wapas standard form mein likh kar khol dena sab se pakki tasdeeq hai. Exam mein waqt kam ho to kam az kam yeh dekh lein ke radius ke andar wala number positive aaya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 4 phir locus ka sawal hai, magar is baar faaslon ke saath. Plan hamesha ek hi hota hai: chalte hue point ko \(P(x, y)\) kaho; di hui sharat ko distance formula se equation mein badlo; simplify karo. Agar nateeje mein \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients barabar hon, \(xy\) term na ho aur \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\) ho, to locus circle hai. Is sawal ko aise bhi socha ja sakta hai: ek keera do kheeliyon A aur B ke darmiyan is tarah chalta hai ke dono se faaslon ke squares ka jama hamesha 4 rahe. Woh kis raaste par chalega? Jawab: ek circle par.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: A point moves so that the sum of the squares of its distances from two points \(A(1, 1)\) and \(B(2, 2)\) is equal to 4. Prove that its locus is a circle.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(1, 1)\), \(B(2, 2)\), aur ek chalta hua point \(P\) jis ke liye \(|\overline{PA}|^{2} + |\overline{PB}|^{2} = 4\).
Maloom karna (saabit karna): \(P\) ka raasta (locus) circle hai.
Tareeqa: locus ke har sawal ki tarah chalte hue point ko \(P(x, y)\) kahenge, sharat ko distance formula se likhenge, simplify karenge, aur dikhayenge ke nateeja circle ki general form hai aur \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\).

Step 1: Sharat (condition) likhein
\[|\overline{PA}|^{2} + |\overline{PB}|^{2} = 4\]
\[\left(\sqrt{(x - 1)^{2} + (y - 1)^{2}}\right)^{2}\]
\[+ \left(\sqrt{(x - 2)^{2} + (y - 2)^{2}}\right)^{2} = 4\]
Kyun: distance formula har faasle ko \(x\) aur \(y\) ki expression bana deta hai; yahi geometry ko algebra mein badalne ka pul hai.

Step 2: Simplify (square aur square root cancel)
\[(x - 1)^{2} + (y - 1)^{2}\]
\[+ (x - 2)^{2} + (y - 2)^{2} = 4\]
Kyun: square root ka square lene se andar wali expression wapas mil jati hai. Sawal ne pehle hi 'squares of distances' kaha tha, is liye root kabhi aata hi nahin.

Step 4: Milte julte terms ikatthe karein
\[2x^{2} + 2y^{2} - 6x - 6y + 10 = 4\]
Kyun: \(x^{2} + x^{2} = 2x^{2}\), \(-2x - 4x = -6x\), aur constants \(1 + 1 + 4 + 4 = 10\); \(y\) ke liye bhi yahi.

Step 5: 2 se divide, phir 2 minus
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 3x - 3y + 5 = 2\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 3x - 3y + 3 = 0\]
Kyun: 2 se divide karne se \(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 ho jate hain (working rule ka Step 1), aur 2 ko left side laane se general form ban jati hai.
Dhyan dein: right side ke 4 ko bhi 2 se divide karna hai, warna 5 = 4 jaisi ghalti ho jati hai.

Step 6: Centre aur radius (working rule)
\[2g = -3,\; 2f = -3,\; c = 3\]
\[\text{centre} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{9}{4} - 3} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}\]
\[r = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c = \frac{6}{4} > 0\), is liye yeh asal circle hai; yahi saabit karna tha. (\(\sqrt{3/2}\) ko upar neeche 2 se multiply karne par \(\sqrt{6}/2\) milta hai.)

Tasdeeq:
Circle ka woh point lijiye jo centre ke bilkul right mein hai: \(P = \left(\frac{3}{2} + r, \frac{3}{2}\right)\), jahan \(r^{2} = \frac{3}{2}\).
\[|PA|^{2} = \left(\tfrac{1}{2} + r\right)^{2} + \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[|PB|^{2} = \left(r - \tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2} + \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[|PA|^{2} + |PB|^{2} = 2r^{2} + 1 = 4\]
Sharat poori ho gayi. Ek dilchasp baat bhi dekhiye: centre \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\) bilkul \(AB\) ka mid-point hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: locus \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 3x - 3y + 3 = 0\) hai, yani circle jis ka centre \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\) aur radius \(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \(2x^{2} + 2y^{2} - 8x + 12y - 6 = 0\) ka centre aur radius nikaaliye.
Step 1: 2 se divide: \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0\).
Step 2: centre \(= \left(-\frac{-4}{2}, -\frac{6}{2}\right) = (2, -3)\).
Step 3: radius \(= \sqrt{4 + 9 - (-3)} = \sqrt{16} = 4\).
Dhyan dein: constant \(-3\) hai, is liye 'constant ghatao' ka matlab \(+3\) hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Sab se pehle \(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 banayein.
2. Centre = (\(x\) ke coefficient ka aadha, sign badal kar; \(y\) ke coefficient ka aadha, sign badal kar).
3. Radius = \(\sqrt{(\text{x ke coefficient ka aadha})^{2} + (\text{y ke coefficient ka aadha})^{2} - \text{constant}}\).
4. Locus: \(P(x, y)\) lo, sharat ko distance formula se likho, simplify karo, phir centre aur radius parho.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} + 20x + \dots\) par 5 se divide kiye baghair Steps 2-3 laga dena: is se centre \((-10, \dots)\) aata hai, jo ghalat hai.
2. Centre mein coefficient ka sign na badalna: \(x\) ka coefficient \(+4\) ho to centre ka pehla coordinate \(-2\) hai.
3. Common coefficient se sirf kuch terms ko divide karna; har term ko divide karna zaroori hai.
